nodes.label: command message
nodes.def: A message that encodes an invocation of an operation on the receiver, carrying method name and arguments.

nodes.label: message channel
nodes.def: A virtual pipeline through which messages travel from sender to receiver; analogous to a typed stream or queue.

nodes.label: datatype channel
nodes.def: A channel dedicated to one message type, enforcing contract clarity at the channel level rather than inside the payload.

nodes.label: message
nodes.def: A discrete packet of information sent over a channel, carrying a payload and metadata for routing and processing.

nodes.label: message router
nodes.def: A component that inspects message content or metadata and forwards the message to one or more downstream channels.

nodes.label: aggregator
nodes.def: A router that collects related messages over time and combines them into a single coherent output message.

nodes.label: content based router
nodes.def: A router that examines message payload fields to determine the destination channel, decoupling sender from destination knowledge.

nodes.label: request reply
nodes.def: A message exchange pattern pairing an outgoing request message with a correlated response message returned to the original sender.

nodes.label: cp purge action
nodes.def: The execution step that removes qualifying messages from the channel: permanent deletion, move to dead_letter_channel, or quarantine to invalid_message_channel.

nodes.label: dead letter channel
nodes.def: A channel where messages go after exhausting retries, signaling a delivery failure requiring intervention.

nodes.label: dm 001
nodes.def: payload_structure: The internal data shape of a document message, comprising typed fields and nested data elements that constitute the complete business data being transmitted.

nodes.label: dm 002
nodes.def: semantic_envelope: Metadata wrapper around the payload describing document provenance, intent classification, and temporal context without prescribing receiver action.

nodes.label: guaranteed delivery
nodes.def: The assurance that a message sent over a channel will eventually be delivered, even if the receiver is temporarily unavailable.

nodes.label: message store
nodes.def: A durable repository of all messages processed by an integration component, enabling replay and audit trails.

nodes.label: message transformer
nodes.def: A component that modifies message structure or content as it passes through, translating between producer and consumer schemas.

nodes.label: integration style
nodes.def: A coarse-grained approach to system interconnection, defined by the mechanism used to move data between systems.

nodes.label: message broker
nodes.def: Middleware that holds a central registry of channels, routes messages between them, and manages subscriber lifecycles.

nodes.label: message historian
nodes.def: A component that archives all messages passing through a channel for compliance, auditing, or forensic replay.

nodes.label: dm 003
nodes.def: business_object_type: A typed classifier identifying the kind of business entity the document represents, such as purchase_order, invoice, or shipment_manifest.

nodes.label: document message
nodes.def: A message that carries a complete data payload (e.g. a purchase order) without prescribing what the receiver must do.

nodes.label: event message
nodes.def: A message that notifies the receiver something has happened, typically carrying a lightweight notification payload.

nodes.label: idempotent consumer
nodes.def: A consumer designed to safely process the same message more than once without side effects, essential for guaranteed delivery.

nodes.label: messaging system
nodes.def: Middleware infrastructure that provides channels, routing, and delivery guarantees for asynchronous message transport.

nodes.label: publish subscribe channel
nodes.def: A channel where one publisher sends and all subscribed receivers consume; each gets its own copy of the message.

nodes.label: schema validation
nodes.def: The enforcement that a message payload conforms to its declared schema before it is routed or transformed.

nodes.label: splitter
nodes.def: A router that breaks a composite message containing multiple items into individual messages, one per item.

nodes.label: canonical data model
nodes.def: A standardized, technology-agnostic message schema used across the enterprise to avoid direct dependency on any system's native format.

nodes.label: channel adapter
nodes.def: A connector that bridges external systems or protocols into a messaging channel, encapsulating the legacy system's API.

nodes.label: cp threshold condition
nodes.def: A predicate over channel_state_snapshot values that evaluates to true when purge_trigger should fire, such as depth_overflow or stale_age_exceeded.

nodes.label: dm 004
nodes.def: document_schema: A formal contract defining the expected payload_structure fields, their types, cardinality, and optionality for a given business_object_type.

nodes.label: dm 005
nodes.def: content_identifier: A stable unique reference (document_id, correlation token) that identifies this specific document instance across systems and message stores.

nodes.label: message type registry
nodes.def: A catalog that maps message type names or namespace identifiers to their schemas and handlers in the integration system.

nodes.label: messaging integration
nodes.def: Integration via asynchronous message passing through a message broker, decoupling sender and receiver in time and space.

nodes.label: normalizer
nodes.def: A transformer that reconciles multiple inbound message formats into a single canonical format before routing.

nodes.label: wire tap
nodes.def: A system management pattern that taps into a channel to observe messages without disrupting the normal flow.

nodes.label: bulk message consumer
nodes.def: A consumer that collects multiple messages over a batching window and processes them together for throughput optimization.

nodes.label: circuit breaker
nodes.def: A resilience pattern that stops forwarding requests to a failing downstream system after a threshold of failures is exceeded.

nodes.label: claim check
nodes.def: A transformation that stores the full message body in an external store and replaces it with a lightweight reference token in the message.

nodes.label: command priority
nodes.def: A metadata field indicating the urgency or precedence level of a command message, used by schedulers and routers to order or filter command processing.

nodes.label: command target
nodes.def: The logical or physical destination endpoint to which a command message is addressed, specifying which receiver should process the invocation.

nodes.label: command timeout
nodes.def: The maximum duration a sender will wait for a command to complete before considering it failed; exceeding this triggers timeout handling or retry.

nodes.label: composed message processor
nodes.def: A processor that splits an incoming composite message, routes each part through separate paths, then aggregates the results.

nodes.label: content enricher
nodes.def: A transformer that supplements an incoming message with additional data fetched from an external source before forwarding.

nodes.label: correlation identifier
nodes.def: A unique ID placed on both request and reply messages so the sender can match responses to their originating calls.

nodes.label: cp poison message
nodes.def: A message that has caused repeated processing failures or is structurally unprocessable and blocks channel progress if retained.

nodes.label: cp purge history
nodes.def: An audit log recording which messages were purged, when, under which policy, and the channel_state_snapshot at purge time for replay and tuning.

nodes.label: cp purge policy
nodes.def: A set of rules defining which messages qualify for purging: age threshold, retry exhaustion, poison detection criteria, or pattern matching on content.

nodes.label: cp purge scheduler
nodes.def: The component that periodically evaluates threshold_condition and, when true, dispatches purge_action against the target channel.

nodes.label: cp purge trigger
nodes.def: A condition that initiates a channel purge cycle; may be time-based, count-based, or event-based such as threshold_exceeded.

nodes.label: cp stale message
nodes.def: A message that has exceeded its relevance window or idle duration and no longer carries actionable data for downstream consumers.

nodes.label: dm 007
nodes.def: document_origin: Metadata identifying the originating system, agent, or process that produced the document_message.

nodes.label: dm 009
nodes.def: schema_registry_entry: An entry in the message_type_registry binding a business_object_type to its document_schema and authorized handlers.

nodes.label: end to end acknowledge
nodes.def: A correlation pattern where the final consumer sends an acknowledgment that propagates back through the routing chain to the original sender.

nodes.label: envelope wrapper
nodes.def: A transformer that wraps or unwraps a message in an envelope to add or strip protocol-level headers for transport.

nodes.label: event driven architecture
nodes.def: An architectural style where system components react to events published to a message bus rather than being invoked directly.

nodes.label: event subscription
nodes.def: The registration of a consumer's interest in receiving messages from a particular channel or topic based on content or type.

nodes.label: exactly once delivery
nodes.def: Message delivery semantics ensuring that a message is processed precisely one time, combining delivery guarantees with deduplication.

nodes.label: fault payload
nodes.def: A data envelope containing error details returned when an operation fails, typically including fault code, description, and optional context for recovery.

nodes.label: health check endpoint
nodes.def: A monitoring interface that exposes integration component status (channels healthy, queues depth, processing lag) for observability.

nodes.label: invalid message channel
nodes.def: A channel that captures malformed or unprocessable messages for manual inspection instead of blocking the main flow.

nodes.label: message datatype
nodes.def: The classification or schema identifier of a message that determines which datatype channels it can traverse.

nodes.label: message expiration
nodes.def: A property on a message indicating it becomes invalid after a certain time and should be discarded if not delivered.

nodes.label: messaging gateway
nodes.def: A Façade that exposes integration functionality to internal clients while hiding the underlying messaging API and complexity.

nodes.label: messaging translator
nodes.def: A bridge component that converts between the enterprise's canonical data model and the external system's proprietary format.

nodes.label: point to point channel
nodes.def: A channel with exactly one consumer per message; guarantees that exactly one receiver processes each message.

nodes.label: process manager
nodes.def: A stateful component that orchestrates a multi-step business process by sending messages to channels and handling responses.

nodes.label: recipient list
nodes.def: A router that sends the same message to a list of recipients computed at runtime from the message content or context.

nodes.label: remote procedure invocation
nodes.def: Integration where one system exposes a callable API and another synchronously invokes it as if it were local.

nodes.label: resequencer
nodes.def: A router that reorders a stream of messages into the correct sequence before passing them downstream.

nodes.label: result payload
nodes.def: A data envelope containing the return value or outcome produced by a successfully executed operation, structured to match the expected response schema.

nodes.label: return address
nodes.def: Metadata on a reply message indicating which channel and possibly which queue the response should be routed to.

nodes.label: scatter gather
nodes.def: A router that broadcasts a request to multiple recipients and then collects and consolidates all their responses.

nodes.label: transactional integration
nodes.def: Integration that groups message production or consumption with local database updates into a single atomic unit of work.

nodes.label: type matching check
nodes.def: The validation that a message's actual type matches a datatype channel's declared type at the point of send or receive.

nodes.label: type schema binding
nodes.def: The linkage between a datatype channel and the formal schema or structure definition of its accepted message type.

nodes.label: untyped channel
nodes.def: A channel without a declared datatype that accepts messages of any type, serving as the contrast to datatype channels.

nodes.label: asynchronous messaging
nodes.def: Messaging semantics where the sender does not block waiting for the receiver to process the message before continuing.

nodes.label: at least once delivery
nodes.def: Message delivery semantics where a message is retried until acknowledged, guaranteeing delivery but allowing possible duplicates.

nodes.label: at most once delivery
nodes.def: Message delivery semantics where a message may be lost but is never redelivered; sender does not retry on failure.

nodes.label: attachment
nodes.def: Secondary data elements or files appended to the document message beyond its primary business payload.

nodes.label: canonical form
nodes.def: The normalized or standardized representation of the document after transformation, serving as the canonical data format.

nodes.label: channel bridge
nodes.def: A connection point that joins two channel segments or a channel to an external system, enabling message flow across the boundary while preserving channel semantics.

nodes.label: channel purger
nodes.def: A system management pattern that periodically clears a channel of stale or poison messages to reset system state.

nodes.label: channel type declaration
nodes.def: The explicit binding of a message datatype to a channel at channel creation or configuration time, establishing the type contract.

nodes.label: channel typing discipline
nodes.def: The classification of datatype channels by typing rigor: static typing enforces type at compile/build time, dynamic typing enforces at message inspection time.

nodes.label: choreography
nodes.def: A decentralized integration style where each system knows only its own part of the process; there is no central orchestrator.

nodes.label: cmd 001
nodes.def: operation_identifier — the name or qualified identifier of the operation being invoked on the receiver

nodes.label: cmd 002
nodes.def: operation_arguments — structured data representing the parameters passed to the invoked operation

nodes.label: cmd 003
nodes.def: command_target — the destination endpoint service or receiver on which the operation is to be executed

nodes.label: cmd 004
nodes.def: command_priority — urgency level that influences routing queue ordering and processor scheduling

nodes.label: cmd 005
nodes.def: idempotency_key — unique value the receiver uses to detect and suppress duplicate command executions

nodes.label: cmd 006
nodes.def: command_timeout — duration after which the sender abandons waiting for execution result

nodes.label: cmd 007
nodes.def: target_interface_version — version identifier enabling the receiver to select the correct operation contract

nodes.label: cmd 008
nodes.def: execution_context — metadata about the calling environment such as principal identity and correlation scope

nodes.label: cmd 009
nodes.def: result_payload — data returned by successful command execution part of request_reply exchange

nodes.label: cmd 010
nodes.def: fault_payload — structured error information returned when command execution fails part of request_reply

nodes.label: content filter
nodes.def: A transformer that removes unwanted fields from a message, reducing payload size or stripping sensitive data.

nodes.label: content integrity
nodes.def: A cryptographic checksum or hash value computed over the document content to detect unauthorized alterations in transit.

nodes.label: content router for documents
nodes.def: The application of content_based_router to a document_message using payload fields to determine routing destination.

nodes.label: cp channel state snapshot
nodes.def: A point-in-time capture of channel metrics (depth, oldest_message_age, error_rate) used to evaluate purge_policy conditions before triggering a purge.

nodes.label: cp retention window
nodes.def: A configurable time interval after which messages become stale_message candidates for purging; part of purge_policy definition.

nodes.label: delayer
nodes.def: A router that holds messages for a configurable duration before forwarding them, implementing delayed delivery semantics.

nodes.label: detour
nodes.def: A system management pattern that reroutes messages through a debugging or inspection step before resuming normal delivery.

nodes.label: dm 006
nodes.def: processing_hint: An optional non-directive annotation suggesting preferred handling, urgency, or routing preference without constituting a command.

nodes.label: dm 008
nodes.def: payload_extractor: A component that retrieves specific fields from the payload_structure for routing, correlation, or downstream transformation.

nodes.label: doc payload
nodes.def: The complete data content carried by a document_message, representing the full information payload without prescribing receiver action.

nodes.label: document classifier
nodes.def: A component or rule set that examines document content to determine its payload type category for downstream routing.

nodes.label: document content
nodes.def: The actual business data carried by the document message, constituting the primary payload that the receiver processes.

nodes.label: document distinguishes from command
nodes.def: document_message differs from command_message by carrying data rather than prescribing method invocations.

nodes.label: document semantic type
nodes.def: The domain-specific classification of a document_message payload, distinguishing purchase orders from invoices or other business documents.

nodes.label: durable subscriber
nodes.def: A subscriber registration that survives broker restarts; undelivered messages are queued and delivered once the subscriber reconnects.

nodes.label: dynamic router
nodes.def: A router that consults a registry or lookup table at runtime to determine destinations, allowing routing rules to change without redeployment.

nodes.label: enterprise service bus
nodes.def: An architectural platform that combines messaging, routing, transformation, and protocol bridging into a single integration middleware layer.

nodes.label: execution context
nodes.def: A structured record of runtime state passed alongside a command, providing the environment information needed to correctly process the operation invocation.

nodes.label: file transfer integration
nodes.def: Integration via shared filesystem where each system produces/consumes files, requiring conventions on naming and polling.

nodes.label: idempotency key
nodes.def: A unique identifier assigned to a command that allows receivers to detect and discard duplicate submissions, ensuring safe retries without double execution.

nodes.label: list of interceptors
nodes.def: A system management pattern that registers interceptor objects to run before or after message processing for cross-cutting concerns.

nodes.label: load balancer
nodes.def: A router that distributes messages across multiple equivalent receiver instances to spread processing load.

nodes.label: message filter
nodes.def: A router that discards messages that do not meet a predicate condition, suppressing unwanted messages from downstream consumers.

nodes.label: operation arguments
nodes.def: The parameter values supplied to the operation being invoked by a command message, structured according to the target interface's argument schema.

nodes.label: operation identifier
nodes.def: A named or coded reference that uniquely identifies which operation a command message is requesting, mapping to a procedure on the target system.

nodes.label: orchestration
nodes.def: A centralized integration style where a single process manager directs the sequence of operations across multiple services.

nodes.label: polling consumer
nodes.def: A consumer that repeatedly queries a source for new messages rather than receiving them push-style from a channel.

nodes.label: routing slip
nodes.def: A routing pattern where each message carries its own itinerary of processing steps, executed in sequence by participating nodes.

nodes.label: sequential convoy
nodes.def: A routing pattern that correlates messages across multiple channels by a shared sequencing key to maintain order across streams.

nodes.label: shared database integration
nodes.def: Integration via a common relational schema where systems read/write shared tables as the coupling mechanism.

nodes.label: smart proxy
nodes.def: A component that monitors a channel and takes corrective action (e.g., resends, redirects) when abnormal conditions are detected.

nodes.label: target interface version
nodes.def: A version descriptor indicating which contract version of the target interface a command message adheres to, enabling version-aware routing and validation.

nodes.label: test message
nodes.def: A system management pattern that injects a known probe message into the flow to verify correct processing downstream.

nodes.label: throttler
nodes.def: A router that limits the rate at which messages pass through, protecting downstream systems from overload.

nodes.label: type constraint enforcement
nodes.def: The runtime or compile-time rule that a datatype channel accepts only messages whose datatype matches the declared type, rejecting mismatched messages.

nodes.label: type metadata
nodes.def: The descriptor carried by a datatype channel identifying the exact message type, schema, or format that the channel transports.

nodes.label: type safe consumer
nodes.def: A message consumer bound to a datatype channel that receives only messages of the declared datatype, enabling type-safe processing without runtime type checks.

nodes.label: type safe producer
nodes.def: A message producer bound to a datatype channel that can only publish messages of the declared datatype, preventing accidental type violations.

nodes.label: document distinguishes from event
nodes.def: document_message differs from event_message by carrying complete business data rather than lightweight occurrence notifications.

nodes.label: document envelope
nodes.def: A transport wrapper bundling document content with its metadata, headers, and routing information for channel delivery.

nodes.label: document historian
nodes.def: The use of message_historian to archive document_message exchanges for compliance and forensic analysis.

nodes.label: document identifier
nodes.def: A unique reference assigned to a document_message enabling correlation, lookup, and idempotent processing.

nodes.label: document identity
nodes.def: A unique identifier or business key that uniquely distinguishes one document instance from all others in the integration system.

nodes.label: document message is message
nodes.def: document_message specializes the general concept of message, inheriting channel transport, headers, and delivery semantics.

nodes.label: document metadata
nodes.def: Auxiliary descriptors attached to a document_message describing origin, timestamp, version, or business context.

nodes.label: document reference
nodes.def: A link or pointer to related documents, enabling document graphs and cross-referencing within the message stream.

nodes.label: document store
nodes.def: The use of message_store to persist document_message payloads enabling audit trails and replay capability.

nodes.label: enterprise integration pattern
nodes.def: A reusable solution template for connecting distributed systems, codified from real-world middleware and messaging experience.

nodes.label: message bridge
nodes.def: An adapter linking two messaging systems or channel types so messages flow across heterogeneous middleware.

nodes.label: non prescriptive behavior
nodes.def: The semantic trait distinguishing document_message from command_message, indicating the receiver determines its own response.

nodes.label: normalizer for documents
nodes.def: The use of normalizer to reconcile incoming document_message payloads from varying formats into a canonical schema.

nodes.label: payload completeness
nodes.def: The defining property of a document_message asserting the payload contains all necessary data for the consumer to act upon voluntarily.

nodes.label: payload encoding
nodes.def: The serialization format of the document_message payload, such as JSON, XML, YAML, or binary encoding.

nodes.label: payload schema
nodes.def: The structural definition that a document_message payload conforms to, specifying fields, types, and constraints.

nodes.label: payload type
nodes.def: A classification identifier indicating the document category or business object type, enabling routing and handler selection.

nodes.label: payload validation
nodes.def: The process of verifying that document content conforms to its declared payload schema before further processing.

nodes.label: schema validation on document
nodes.def: The application of schema_validation to ensure document_message payloads conform to their declared payload_schema.

nodes.label: static recipient list
nodes.def: A recipient list with fixed destinations known at design time, compiled into the routing logic rather than derived from content.
